column1: # Measured peak memory of a single Lean module, in megabytes of peak resident set size.
# DESIGN.md:966 -- "no single reduction command should be allowed to become the memory boundary for
# an entire paper" -- is enforced by scripts/check_decide_budget.py against this file.  Where a
# module has a row here the number is AUTHORITATIVE and the checker's static payload proxy is not
# consulted for it; measuring a module is therefore the way to retire a proxy complaint honestly.
# APPEND-ONLY, so a janitor's remote run can add a row mechanically and never rewrite history:
#   printf 'module\t%s\t%d\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
#     "$module" "$peak_mb" "$(date -u +%F)" "$host" "$tool" "$note" \
#     >> scripts/decide_memory_budget.tsv
# Tab-separated.  Lines starting with '#' and blank lines are ignored.  Columns:
#   1 kind     'module' for one module; 'family' for a trailing-'*' glob over module names.
#              A 'module' row always wins over a 'family' row for the same module, however old,
#              because it is the more specific statement.
#   2 key      module name (dotted), or module-name glob ending in '*'.
#   3 peak_mb  integer peak RSS in MB.
#   4 date     ISO-8601 YYYY-MM-DD.  The NEWEST row for a key wins, so a module whose reduction was
#              made cheaper is retired by APPENDING its new lower number, never by editing a line.
#   5 host     provenance of the measurement.
#   6 tool     how it was measured.
#   7 note     free-form.
# HOW TO MEASURE.  On macOS:   /usr/bin/time -l lake env lean <File>.lean   (peak is bytes)
#                  On Linux:   /usr/bin/time -v lake env lean <File>.lean   (Maximum resident set)
# Divide macOS bytes by 1048576.  Measure ONE module with an otherwise warm .lake, single worker
# (`LEAN_NUM_THREADS=1`), so the number is the module's own peak and not the build's.
# UNATTRIBUTED FIGURES FROM 2026-08-28, recorded here as prose because they were never resolved to
# a per-module key and this file must not invent one:
#   * The Edge family measured 7.3-19.6 GB per module, median 15.2 GB.  The family row below
#     records the measured MAXIMUM, which is the only figure that is true of the family as a whole.
#   * "A4 closure" peaked at 3319 MB.  No module or glob in this repository was identified as that
#     closure, so it gets no row; it is under the 6000 MB budget either way.
#   * Modules outside these families were typically under 3000 MB.
# kind
module
module
family
